title: Interactive Gambling Amendment (Stop the Gambling Ads) Bill 2026
short_title: Interactive Gambling Amendment (Stop the Gambling Ads) Bill 2026

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would progressively prohibit advertising of licensed interactive wagering services across broadcasting, online platforms, other media and sporting venues, reaching a comprehensive ban after three years.

Initial restrictions would cover online and social media advertisements, news and current affairs broadcasts, and commercial radio advertising during specified morning and afternoon school travel periods.

Exceptions would cover political communications, specified factual business information, harm reduction messages and other defined activities, with a temporary exemption for small community radio services.
changes: From the first anniversary, restrictions would extend to live sport, surrounding odds promotion and stadium advertising.
From the second anniversary, broadcasting and datacasting advertisements would be prohibited between 6:00 am and 10:00 pm.
The full advertising prohibition would operate from the third anniversary, subject to the specified exceptions.
Breaching the advertising prohibitions could result in criminal prosecution or civil penalties.
The Australian Communications and Media Authority could investigate breaches and use warnings, infringement notices and injunctions.
summary.affected: Licensed wagering providers, advertisers, broadcasters, online publishers, sporting bodies and the communications regulator are affected.
